commit.message: Align efficiency scoring with the agent turn budget
Exclude patch debris from source change detection
Add Tool-Agnostic Source Change Detection
Update source-change assertion wording
Detect Source Changes After Agent Runs
Record agent source changes during rebuild
Clarify source-change evidence requirements

Document both providers, their keys, and how to verify one

Covers .env for GEMINI_API_KEY and VYCE_API_KEY, provider selection via
SRELAB_AGENT_PROVIDER, the per-provider model variables, and the shared
tuning knobs.

Includes a pre-run verification recipe, because a zero-balance Vyce account
returns HTTP 200 with a valid envelope and completion_tokens: 0 rather than
an error -- indistinguishable from a broken model or a broken integration,
and it cost several debugging cycles to identify. Also notes that rateLimit
is requests/min, not credit, and that a model must support tool calling to
drive the agent at all.

Point tests at the provider-neutral classes

Follows the type moves and renames: the evidence tests now exercise
EvidenceGate directly rather than through a provider instance, the memory
test tracks the ToolSafeChatMemory rename, and AgentSettings.atLeastInt
replaces the moved helper.

AgentFactoryTest no longer reads defaults back off a constructed agent.
SRELAB_VYCE_MODEL and SRELAB_VYCE_BASE_URL are real overrides, so that made
the test pass or fail depending on the shell running the build -- the same
ambient-config trap that once sent a Claude model name to the Gemini
endpoint. It asserts the documented constants instead, and only checks an
instance when nothing overrides them.

Record which provider and model served a run

A score is meaningless without knowing what produced it. With two providers
wired up -- and a Vyce routing pseudo-model ('auto') that picks a model per
request -- a report naming neither could not be compared against another
report, and a failed run could not be attributed.

Adds agentProvider/agentModel, populated from the live agent. A 21-arg
compatibility constructor keeps previously archived runs loading, with both
fields null: those runs genuinely never recorded what served them.

Verify tool-call capability before a run spends anything

Adds ToolCallPreflight: one cheap call with a throwaway tool, asserting the
configured model emits a native tool call. The agent can only act through
tools, so a model that will not emit them cannot drive a run at all -- yet
three models were observed failing that way (one narrated calls as prose,
one replied 'no tools are currently available', one emitted calls then went
silent). Each cost a full sandbox, database and target deploy to discover,
and each was reported as an agent that failed rather than a model that
never acted.

Staged so it gates only the agent step, not the pipeline:
  - autoStartAgent (CLI): checked before setup, where failing early
    genuinely saves a sandbox.
  - GUI: checked at Start Agent. Steps 1-5 need no LLM, so a provider
    outage must not stop code import, build or fault injection, and a
    built sandbox with an injected fault is useful on its own.

Rate-limit errors are never retried -- another attempt adds to the same
limit, and retrying turned each blocked run into three provider calls.
SRELAB_AGENT_PREFLIGHT=off skips the check.

Also makes triggerAgent idempotent and cleanup run once. The phase check
was check-then-act, so concurrent Start Agent clicks each began an agent
over one sandbox; the first to fail tore the container down while the
others were still issuing tool calls, flooding the log with
'No such container'.

Add the provider-neutral agent classes the refactor depends on

The refactor that made SreRunAgent provider-neutral was committed without
these files, so HEAD did not compile: SreRunAgent, AgentReActLoop and
VyceAgent all referenced types that existed only as untracked working-tree
files. Verified by compiling a clean worktree of HEAD, which failed with
'cannot find symbol' across all three.

  EvidencePolicy, AgentRunResult, AgentExecutionException
      Formerly nested inside the Gemini agent, so the interface every
      provider implements depended on one concrete provider.
  EvidenceGate      the honesty check, shared so no provider can get a
                    weaker bar than another.
  AgentPrompts      the opening observation, shared so providers open a
                    run with byte-identical wording.
  AgentSettings     turn/token/timeout/memory/mode knobs, parsed once
                    instead of duplicated per provider.
  GeminiAgent       the Gemini provider, renamed from AIAgent for
                    symmetry with VyceAgent.

Add regression test for the rebuild turn-count double-charge

Confirms rebuildAndRedeploy() now adds exactly one transcript entry
for a successful build+restart, and that calling restartApplication()
directly (independent of a rebuild) still records its own entry --
only the nested call is exempt.

Verified this test actually catches the bug it targets: reverted the
prior commit's SandboxTools.java change locally and re-ran the test,
which failed with 'expected: <1> but was: <2>', confirming it detects
the exact regression before restoring the fix.

Stop double-counting rebuildAndRedeploy's internal restart

rebuildAndRedeploy() called the public restartApplication() tool
internally to load newly compiled code, and that method wrote its own
transcript entry. Since turnsUsed is read directly as
AgentTranscript.commandCount(), a rebuild+restart -- one decision by
the agent -- was billed as two turns, costing real efficiency-score
points on every SOURCE-mode run that reached a rebuild.

Split restartApplication() into the public @Tool method (still one
transcript entry per direct call) and a private doRestartApplication()
helper with no transcript side effects. rebuildAndRedeploy() now calls
the untracked helper directly.

Verified against the archived 98/100 run: recomputing its score with
the corrected turn count (6 instead of 7) yields 99/100.

Fix agent resolution pipeline and evaluator scoring

- Pass in-container health URL (localhost:8080) to the agent instead of
  the host-mapped port, which was unreachable from inside the container
  and caused curl exit=7 on every health check.
- Wait for the app to become healthy after restartApplication() so the
  agent doesn't check health mid-startup and give up.
- Stop readLogs from reading /proc/1/fd/1 (a live pipe that blocks until
  the exec timeout fires); only tail static log paths.
- Forbid launching the app via executeShellCommand in the tool docs.
- Rework Evaluator scoring so a genuinely-resolved run no longer floors
  to 0 after 50s / 10 commands.
- Reuse a shared DockerClient in SandboxManager instead of building one
  per exec/restart call.
- Run connection-pool-exhaustion holds on background threads so pg_sleep
  no longer blocks the injector.
